description: Robot Glove Hand v1: a 3D-printable TENDON-actuated robotic hand built around Jake's hand model. DEPENDS ON voice-0c526dc0: start only once its hand comfort-volume model (cad/openscad/glove_hand) and fit-test surround have landed. If they aren't there yet, say so and stop. Goal: a hollow exoskeleton-style hand that Jake's hand fits inside (thin TPU layer on the palm side, tendons, servos and routing on the back), which the robot can also use. Same left-hand layout as the Aero Hand. Study existing open-source tendon hands and reuse what fits: Aero Hand Open (Chestnut-Robotics/aero-hand-open, our current hand), LEAP Hand, ORCA Hand, Amazing Hand (Pollen), InMoov, DexHand, OpenBionics/Hero arm, soft exo-gloves. Record every reference (repo URL, license, what was borrowed) in cad/openscad/glove_hand/REFERENCES.md and respect the licenses. OpenSCAD, parameterized on the hand model so either side can change independently. Generations kept as labeled files. Dual-render compare (voice-8fe317cd), shown on the Designs page.

results.notes: Jake decided: design it FROM SCRATCH. No geometry or files copied from other projects. The agent may study open-source hands for ideas only (tendon routing, pulley sizing, printable joint and pin tolerances) and should still note in REFERENCES.md which ideas came from where.

user_request.name: once that agent finishes up I want you to have another one taking that and attempting to build a 3D printable robotic hand out of it. It should be tendon actuated. Reference any existing open source projects and record their reference to them.

summary: Design a 3D-printable, tendon-driven robot hand in OpenSCAD that Jake's hand fits inside, using the Aero Hand's left-hand layout. Everything must be designed from scratch, with open-source hands studied only for ideas, each credited by project in REFERENCES.md.
